title: The Folly of Self-Defense
speaker: Pastor Tito Lyro

outline.title: A Father's Godly Jealousy
subpoints: Paul defends himself not for personal glory but for the sake of the gospel
The church is betrothed to Christ as a chaste virgin
Warning against the corruption of the mind by the serpent's craftiness

outline.title: A Counterfeit Christ
subpoints: False apostles preach another Jesus and a different spirit
Tolerance of false teaching is a failure to reject the lie
The primary standard for judging a church is the exaltation of Christ

outline.title: A Free Gospel
subpoints: Paul humbled himself to exalt the Corinthians
The gospel was preached free of charge to avoid being a burden
Paul’s integrity is proven by his financial independence from the church

outline.title: A Disguised Enemy
subpoints: False apostles transform themselves into apostles of Christ
Satan disguises himself as an angel of light
Ministers of righteousness who are actually ministers of Satan

summary:
In this sermon, Pastor Tito Lyro examines 2 Corinthians 11:1-15, focusing on the necessity of self-defense when the integrity of the gospel is threatened. He illustrates Paul’s motivation through the metaphor of a father’s godly jealousy, where Paul views the Corinthian church as a bride betrothed to Christ. This spiritual jealousy is not rooted in personal ego but in a deep concern that the congregation’s minds might be corrupted by the craftiness of false teachers, leading them away from the simplicity and single-minded focus on Christ.

The message highlights the danger of counterfeit apostles who preach a different Jesus and a different spirit. Pastor Lyro emphasizes that tolerance of such false teaching is a grave spiritual failure, as the primary purpose of the local church is the exaltation of Christ and the proclamation of the true gospel. He contrasts the natural human inclination to be offended by personal slights with the biblical imperative to be deeply offended by lies about the Savior.

Furthermore, the sermon addresses the issue of financial integrity in ministry. Paul’s defense includes his refusal to be a financial burden to the Corinthians, demonstrating that the gospel was preached freely. This stands in stark contrast to false apostles who seek to exploit the church for personal gain. The passage concludes with a warning about the deceptive nature of Satan, who disguises himself as an angel of light, urging believers to discern the true ministers of righteousness from those whose end will be according to their works.
